📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, when the creators and showrunners of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power embarked on season 3, they knew the endgame from the start: The forging of the One Ring. After two seasons in the Second Age of Middle-earth, which saw almost all the other Rings of Power forged—three for Elves, seven for Dwarves, and nine for Men—it was time for Sauron to forge the one to rule them all.

In a recent development, “We wanted a tighter, tauter, more profound season,” claims co-showrunner Patrick McKay, in an interview with Esquire. “We wanted to start with a bang and never let up. We wanted to deepen our characters psychologically, and challenge them in new ways. You’re seeing the end of one part of the story, and the beginning of another.”.

Industry observers note that “We had to have Sauron forge the One Ring,” adds J.D. Payne, who also created and serves as co-showrunner with McKay. “To do that, all the storylines in some way are connected to Sauron’s attempts at world domination. That was the one that so much of our attention and focus went into getting right, and it took all of our departments working together at the top of their games to create.”.

On Wednesday, just in time for Thanksgiving, Prime Video gave Tolkien fans a feast with the final two episodes of The Rings of Power season 3: episode 7, “Orodruin,” and episode 8, “The Doom of Men.”.

Industry observers note that in the penultimate episode, Sauron (Charlie Vickers) learns from the Balrog—who talks, apparently!—how to use the fires of Mount Doom to forge the One Ring. Then, with the power of the One Ring literally in his hands, Sauron mobilizes his army for battle against Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle), the king of Númenor. But instead of a massive, violent bloodbath in the spirit of, say, Game of Thrones, Sauron simply... surrenders. Or does he? We’re talking about a master deceiver, after all.

In a spoiler-filled interview with Esquire, McKay and Payne unpack a few of our biggest questions about season 3, including how and why the Balrog speaks (with actor Simon Pegg lending his voice) to why Pharazôn is actually one of the most consequential figures in the series.

This interview has been edited for clarity.

ESQUIRE: So, wait, the Balrog can talk?

PATRICK MCKAY: One of the things we're constantly trying to do is go deeper into Tolkien’s life's work. He did not just create The Lord of the Rings, he wrote all this other stuff. He envisioned an entire world. It's his legendarium. When you do the deep dive, you find there are surprising things if you only know the book and film trilogy. The Balrog Gandalf faces down in Moria is part of this level of “super being” that is equal to Gandalf and Sauron. They’re Maiar. In prior ages, Balrogs could cast spells and command troops. They’re intelligent. They can talk, you just don’t see that one talk in that circumstance.

The idea of walking out onto a diving board and doing something risky, to show a different side of that being, was something that we felt compelled to do this season. It’s certainly unexpected. We’re always looking to do that. We don’t want to be familiar. We want to show you things in this world that you haven’t seen before.

Talk to me about designing a latest One Ring. Granted, it’s a gold ring; there’s not much you can really deviate. But in what ways did you want to create a One Ring that belongs to The Rings of Power?

In a recent development, MCKAY: The books are pretty specific about the way it looks. It’s a plain gold band. If you’re gonna do that, it’s going to look like the One Ring you’ve seen in other adaptations. We did make a few modifications, just for camera. We broadened it to give it more chunkiness. But it is what it states on the tin.

How is season 3 a culmination of everything that’s happened before, and how is it setting up the rest of the show?

It has been revealed that J.D. PAYNE: It pulls together everything we’ve been doing with Sauron and Galadriel from the first two seasons. In season 1, he befriended her and deceived her in the guise of Halbrand. In season 3, you see Celebrimbor tormenting him: “You’re never gonna be able to make a ring capable of dominating all the other rings—or dominating her.” Part of Sauron’s ambition to forge the One Ring, as a character motivation, is being able to dominate the person who said “no” to him over the last few seasons. You understand how crazy that must have driven him.

According to recent reports, MCKAY: The show’s called Rings of Power, because the creation is the throughline of this entire era of Tolkien’s mythology. At the end of season 3, you’ve now seen the creation of all of them. That’s now the world we live in. Everyone in Middle-earth is a nuclear power, so to speak. Now we’re setting up for the next part of the story, which is, “What are the consequences going to be?” One thing in season 3 we really invested in was Númenor to set Sauron up as the bowling ball crashing into those pins. That’s sort of the beginning of the end of the Second Age. It’s a tragic story. The Rings have an impact on Middle-earth that is felt for thousands of years. Now they are in this world.

The finale is literally titled “The Doom of Men,” and it ends with Sauron “surrendering” to Pharazôn. Or so that’s what he wants them to think. Can you break down this moment? How is this Sauron’s massive chess move?

PAYNE: Everything builds up to that. You’ve seen Gandalf getting through to the Dark Wizard and take out a massive portion of Sauron’s army at the last moment. So the game changes right from underneath him, and he has to make a calculation. Is he going to put all his chips on the table and lose his army in a stalemate? Or is there another way? The great thing about Sauron is that he’s amazing at constructing scenarios that are lose-lose. If he can’t beat Pharazôn on the field of battle, he reasons maybe there’s another way. That’s why the final moment is filled with tension. It’s not simply a surrender. Our Elves, particularly Galadriel, know Sauron so well. She knows this is not a defeat for Sauron, and he’s going to find a way to make this into a play for exactly what he wants. Those who know the lore know what happens when Sauron is taken prisoner to Númenor. We wanted that feeling of dread, watching Charlie Vickers have a hint of a smile.

Sources indicate that one of the most consequential characters this season has been Pharazôn. In what ways does Pharazôn represent the downfall of man?

MCKAY: This is a major character in the mythology. We introduced him in season 1, he’s been sort of a politician gathering power. In season 3, he’s been king for five days, and he’s in his heyday. He’s in his golden era. But he’s driven by insecurity. There was this blacksmith we empowered, who got away, who’s now marching around saying he’s “Lord.” No, I’m the guy! There’s professional jealousy there.

We talk sometimes about how he’s Stalin to Sauron’s Hitler. You’ve got two characters who are quite full of themselves, and have a high opinion of themselves, which puts them on a trajectory. Pharazôn’s goal is, “I want to take on Sauron.” That makes him a compelling character because you watch the way he greases the wheels and maneuvers to bring about that end. We give a lot of credit to our actor, Trystan Gravelle. He leaps off the screen in season 3.

Speaking of showdowns, one of the biggest confrontations you stage in season 3 is between Sauron and Gandalf, which Tolkien never wrote in the books. What did you hope to discover by pitting these characters together?

It has been revealed that MCKAY: The journey of Gandalf and his involvement with Ciaran Hinds’ character, Pollando, has real deep roots in some Tolkien deep cuts where he talked about wizards who went east and that their activities probably prevented the east from joining Sauron. The story comes from that. We wanted to dramatize that through some of the most iconic characters in the legendarium coming face to face.

PAYNE: Seeing the contrast between them felt like too delicious an opportunity to pass up. Sauron is seeking power at all costs, and Gandalf has been told by the Secret Fire, “To access the greatest power in the universe, you have to give up all other power.” So when Gandalf is offered the world by Sauron, he turns it down. If you demand power, it’s going to destroy you. Ultimately, having the One Ring, and forging it and trying to keep power, sets up the weaknesses of the Third Age that the heroes exploit to finally destroy Sauron.

One of my favorite hobbies is Magic: The Gathering, which has had both Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit as crossover sets. Are there any possibilities for a Rings of Power collaboration?

Recent findings suggest that MCKAY: [Laughs.] No. This is the first we’ve heard about it.

Sources indicate that PAYNE: We actually wrote a draft of a Magic: The Gathering script in the before times. It was one of the last scripts we worked on before turning to Rings of Power. But it was right before the Disney-Fox merger, and it kinda got lost there. But we love that universe.

Recent findings suggest that during her three-day tour of India, the Princess of Wales attended the 2026 Earthshot Prize Ceremony in Mumbai. Prince William founded the initiative in 2020, and it awards environmental solutions with grants to scale and advance their projects.

For the event, Kate wore an oxblood, floor-length Anarkali dress by designer Mahima Mahajan and paired it with extra-fluffy, voluminous bohemian curls pinned in a half-updo.

Sources indicate that an elegant, extra-glossy wavy hairstyle has long been a beauty signature for the princess, often teamed with a side part, hats, or a polished ponytail. But for the green carpet in India, the royal opted for a much more dramatic style that matches the glamorous mood of her outfit, with tighter, cascading bohemian curls woven into a beautiful half-updo twist for a romantic finish.

"I would create these curls using a medium-sized tong," recommends Philipp Haug, co-founder of Haug London Haus salon. "Take relatively small sections and use the tongs with a twisting technique, curling one section away from the face and alternating with one section towards the face throughout. Slightly root stretch when you come to the top of the head instead of curling too close to the scalp.".

To enhance the fluffiness and volume of the curls, shake them out with your fingers instead of combing them.

Your next special occasion hair inspiration, sorted.

  • Industry observers note that A Kidman Carol, his latest play, stemmed from his idea for a spin on the Dickens classic in which Cate Blanchett is visited by Nicole Kidman in order to learn the true meaning of awards season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It started, as things often do for Kevin Zak, as an idea for a meme.

Recent findings suggest that the playwright behind last year’s Ginger Twinsies, a Millennial satire of The Parent Trap, is more widely known for his presence on social media, where his pop culture memes sit right at the corner of Extremely Online and Incredibly Gay. (This likely had something to do, he admits, with growing up with two gay brothers and a father who would decorate their front door with a giant Academy Award cutout on Oscars night.).

Industry observers note that A Kidman Carol, his latest play, stemmed from his idea for a spin on the Dickens classic in which Cate Blanchett is visited by Nicole Kidman in order to learn the true meaning of awards season. When a friend who runs the Alleyway Theatre in Buffalo, New York, offered a few nights to workshop anything he wanted in 2024, Zak knew just the holiday program he wanted to see.

It has been revealed that enter Marla Mindelle and Josh Sharp, who now play Kidman and Blanchett in the show’s off-Broadway premiere. As Mindelle puts it, “The world of theater is so small, off-Broadway even smaller, and alt queer comedy is literally a basement limited to about 10 people, and we are three out of those 10.” She has a point: Mindelle’s massively popular Titanique and Sharp’s A24-backed film Dicks: The Musical both started at (literally) underground comedy clubs.

In a recent development, when Zak asked them if they’d like to participate in a workshop presentation that took place last winter, Mindelle claims she and Sharp texted on the side: “I’ll do it if you do it. It’s five performances. What can go wrong?”.

Sharp and Richard Perez in A Kidman Carol.

“And what can go wrong is a full six-week run at the off-Broadway mall,” Sharp quips, referencing the curious, five-theater layout of New World Stages.

Just in time for the holidays, and with awards season just around the corner, Vogue caught up with the comedy trio to discuss Kidman and Blanchett’s unending star power.

Vogue: Was there ever a question as to which stars you wanted to feature in the show?

Kevin Zak: It was always centered around them.

Industry observers note that josh Sharp: They sort of exemplify this distinction really well, where Cate is more of a “pure actress” who’s like, “Why do I have to make TikToks? I want to act.” And, in the show, we get into how Nicole has leveraged some of that power to be like, “Because I’m a celebrity, I can make all this stuff.” I think because Cate is a person that people know less [about]—you don’t really have a Cate Blanchett impression—she feels a little more like everywoman, and it means we can bend her into being Scrooge. She’s mostly known for her intensity, so she can become a good stand-in for a curmudgeon who wishes the state of the world were different, and Nicole can agree but be a bit more hopeful about it. How do they change each other?

Zak: Besides being all lesbians that have mental breakdowns, Cate’s characters all have the energy of, The world is against me, everyone is trying to get me, like in Tár or Carol or Notes on a Scandal. That feels like a good engine for her throughout the show: As curmudgeonly as she comes across, she’s trying to open your eyes to what the hell is going on, and is anyone going to do anything about it?

This is a very earnestly pro-awards show play. What was the last shockingly good Oscar win?

Marla Mindelle: What if I mentioned Adrian Brody’s second Oscar?

Sharp: What if I mentioned Green Book? There’s gotta be one past this, but my gut goes with Moonlight winning best picture. That was such an affirming culture-stopper to me, where I was like, Thank God we’re allowing movies like that, with zero dollars, to actually win.

Zak: Minari, when Youn Yuh-jung won [for best supporting actress]. Brad Pitt was a producer of the movie and she scolded him for never coming to set during her acceptance speech.

Marla, what have you discovered in your Nicole deep dive?

Recent findings suggest that mindelle: I rewatched To Die For, which I think actually might be my favorite Nicole Kidman film, even over Moulin Rouge!, which I can’t believe I’m saying because Moulin Rouge! was also my sexual awakening. Compared to Cate, I feel like Nicole has 10% more camp. Nicole knows what she is serving and has a little wink about it, like “I know I’m so beautiful and so talented,” where Cate is: “Yes, and I’m also all about the work.”.

Zak: What makes them different in their performances, at least for me, is that Nicole’s characters get hurt and Cate’s characters get mad. In Significant Little Lies, you see this woman in this horrible relationship get hurt, even in her therapy sessions. Even when her therapist is so bluntly truthful with her, all she can really say is, “I think you’re way out of line,” which is a line in our show. Cate is on the defensive. I feel that hurt is disguised with rage, a lot of the time. But that’s what really draws me to them, that core emotional difference. And they’ve never done a movie together, which is so crazy.

When did you each realize Nicole was a star?

Sharp: It was probably Batman Forever.

It has been revealed that zak: Definitely Dr. Chase Meridian in Batman Forever.

In a recent development, mindelle: I remember her having sex in To Die For. That was a pivotal moment where I was like, Oh my God, what is this feeling so sudden and upcoming inside my body? I re-watched it recently and it really is one of the greatest movies ever. She is phenomenal.

Zak: That makes sense. [It’s] why you play her so horny.

Industry observers note that mindelle: It’s not even horny. I just feel like she’s always, like, loose and up for anything.

Mindelle: If you offered her poppers at The Eagle, she’d be like, “Why not?” She’ll do it.

Sharp: I’ve loved The Talented Mr. Ripley since I was young, but I really think Tár is one of the greatest films of the decade. I saw it four times in theaters. I heard people go, “Isn’t it sort of so long and slow and boring?” I’m like, Absolutely, let’s go!

According to recent reports, zak: Notes on a Scandal. I remember going to see it for Judi Dench and then being served Cate Blanchett having a mental breakdown in that press sequence, with her black eyeliner running as she’s just moan-screaming to be left alone. I finally saw myself onscreen.

In writing and preparing for this, were you trying to get into what these women are actually like, or was it all based on their public perception?

Industry observers note that zak: There is a combo of both. Cate, especially, her version of Scrooge is not someone we disagree with, like we do in A Christmas Carol. She makes solid points about the state of, not only the industry, but the planet. She’s been very vocal about her opinions. Her foundation is an anti-AI foundation and, on Las Culturistas, she spoke about how much award season has gotten overblown and how it should be a private event, if we’re going to do it at all. And then, of course, there’s her tirade on leaf blowers and how much she hates them. And then Nicole is truly up for anything, but she also uplifts people. She’s spoken a lot about how she uses her name to uplift young female screenwriters, young female directors, and putting her name on projects so that they get greenlit.

Marla, how’d you develop your insanely good Kidman impression?

According to recent reports, mindelle: The great thing about doing a role like this—a minimal, meaty role like this—is that it’s made me watch a lot of old Nicole Kidman movies. I feel like a kid again because I’m watching all these incredibly nostalgic movies from the ’80s, ’90s, and realizing her body of work is absolutely incredible. And whatever she has become now is almost this camp amalgamation of the past 30 to 40 years of her work. We’re just living in her timeline.

Zak: It feels like there’s never been a dip for Nicole, in terms of movie stardom. She’s only continued to rise in likability, popularity, talent, star power. There was never an era where you thought, Where’d Nicole Kidman go? And on top of being an incredible actress and movie star, she’s now a fashion icon and clubbing in Ibiza, and things like that. She seems like this ethereal presence on earth, which I think gives way for her to be the representation of cinema as ghosts in this show.

Do you have a personal favorite line?

Sharp: “I am Petra’s father” [from Tár].

Industry observers note that mindelle: For me, it’s “That indescribable feeling” [from Kidman’s AMC pre-show ad]. There’s something about her “indescribable” that helped me tap into Nicole.

Zak: Nicole’s laugh. There’s nothing more infectious on screen or in an interview. There’s a super cut of her sneaking up on people on red carpets, where you’ll just see her hand enter the screen and, like, pull Laura Dern closely into her. Nicole’s red carpet star energy is just undeniable and a key thing in the world.

This conversation has been edited and condensed.

#146464. Forget Plymouth Rock This Thanksgiving. American History Is Better Reflected by a Different Stone.

📅 26 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (855 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Esquire ↗ Open Full Page

Forget Plymouth Rock This Thanksgiving. American History Is Better Reflected by a Different Stone.

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Let me send out a little Thanksgiving advice to potential tourists planning to visit us in the Commonwealth (God save it!) in the future.
  • First of all, Plymouth Rock is a boulder in a hole in the ground.
  • Even Alexis de Tocqueville, America’s greatest tourist and, therefore, its primordial sucker, fell for the Rock’s charisma.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let me send out a little Thanksgiving advice to potential tourists planning to visit us in the Commonwealth (God save it!) in the future. If some local tells you to go to see Plymouth Rock, tell them you have tickets for a four-day Duck Tour of the Freedom Trail. I promise you: Seeing Paul Revere’s house four times is infinitely more interesting than seeing Plymouth Rock once.

First of all, Plymouth Rock is a boulder in a hole in the ground. Oh, there’s a classical templish thing above it, but it’s still a boulder in a hole in the ground. Second, there’s almost no historical evidence that any pilgrim feet ever trod upon the rock in question. None of the contemporaneous accounts mention it. It was a nonagenarian named Thomas Faunce who, in 1741, 121 years after the Mayflower arrived, decided that this was the rock on which all the Bradfords and their shipmates disembarked. It moved around Plymouth a lot in the early years. In 1774, it cracked in two, which some folks took as an ill omen for the burgeoning Revolution. (Pieces of it are in the Smithsonian) The year 1620 was carved into the boulder’s surface in 1880. In 1920, it found its permanent home. In 1990, writing in The New Yorker, John McPhee wrote of the rock:.

Even Alexis de Tocqueville, America’s greatest tourist and, therefore, its primordial sucker, fell for the Rock’s charisma.

Sources indicate that damn, Alexis. Have some Madeira and chillez out, mon ami.

If you want to see a genuinely interesting boulder, drive 42 minutes west to the town of Berkley, where you will find Dighton Rock State Park. In another templish building, there is Dighton Rock. It is a six-sided, five-foot-high slab of sandstone. It is also adorned with ancient petroglyphic carvings of uncertain origin. There are depictions of animals and an assortment of lines and whorls and mysterious designs. In 1680, John Danforth got a look at the Dighton Rock and not even his recently bestowed Harvard degree could explain them. He made drawings of the carvings he could see. (At the time Danforth saw it, the rock was partially submerged in the Taunton River.) It also drew the interest of local celebrities like Cotton Mather and poet James Russell Lowell.

Recent findings suggest that danforth’s opinion was that the carvings were made by the local Native tribes, and he thought it depicted an ancient battle of some sort. (If there’s anything like a consensus among people who have studied the carvings, it’s Danforth’s.) However logical that might seem, it didn’t tamp down speculation as the years went by. Down through the centuries, the carvings have been attributed to Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Vikings, Portuguese adventurers, Chinese explorers, and Japanese mariners. And, of course, inevitably … aliens.

Recent findings suggest that however, it was a professor of psychology from Brown University who had the right of it, I think. Edmund Delabarre was a well-respected psychological researcher in the first half of the 20th century. He also grew fascinated with the study of rock carvings in and around Narragansett Bay. Ultimately, his researches brought him to the shores of the Taunton River and to the Dighton Rock.

It has been revealed that ultimately, Delabarre dismissed all the other claims of origin and concluded that the carvings on the Dighton Rock were probably made by a crew sailing under the command of one Miguel Corte-Real, a Portuguese explorer who charted about 600 miles of coastline in and around the Canadian Maritimes. In 1502, Corte-Real set sail for the western Atlantic, seeking to discover what had become of his brother, Gaspar, who had not returned from a voyage to Newfoundland. Miguel vanished, too.

Delabarre’s contention was that Miguel had made it to Upcoming England, and he argued that the inscription was a form of abbreviated Latin that proclaimed Corte-Real to be “king of the Indians.” In his 2017 book The Place of Stone, Douglas Hunter pretty much demolished all of the outre interpretations of the carvings, arguing that the carvings were of Native origin, and that the other interpretations were elements in the erasure of Native history and the legacy of bloody colonization, of which, ironically, the settlement at Plymouth was Ground Zero. The people who didn’t step onshore on a rock in Plymouth introduced one of the first campaigns of the greater American genocide. As Hunter wrote:.

So there’s American history on the Thanksgiving of 2026, ground up between two stones, one a legend with a counterfeit past, and another a mystery with a stolen past. The latter is by far the more compelling. Its history encompasses all of the history, good and bad, of this appropriated continent. Edmund Delabarre was wrong about Miguel Corte-Real and the Portuguese, but he might have been more right than he knew when he wrote that Dighton Rock was a kind of test. In the ambiguity of its carvings at the time of Delabarre’s work, a person saw in them what he wanted to see. Not all of it was pretty, or ennobling, or triumphal. But it's all ours.

In this day and age, it’s almost a rite of passage for a celebrity to have plastic surgery rumors about them swirling online, but Jennifer Lawrence has been speaking her truth on the matter as of late.

Last week on Watch What Happens Live, the Hunger Games actress casually slipped into her conversation with host Andy Cohen that she has upcoming breast implants and even credited her plastic surgeon, Steven Teitelbaum, for the “full C” cups.

Recent findings suggest that she continues to set the record straight on her cosmetic procedures—this time shutting down rumors that she had a blepharoplasty. Online rumors swiftly speculated that Lawrence had undergone upper eyelid surgery, but her latest Instagram post shuts them down. Her makeup artist, Shayna Gold, shared a mailer of products from the actress’s new haircare line, Mes, and Lawrence reposted the photo to her own story with a cheeky caption. “Iykyk she’s the one who did my bleph,” Lawrence wrote, crediting Gold and pointing to makeup as the reason she looks so wide awake, officially poking holes in any eyelid surgery rumors.

Industry observers note that lawrence has previously been open about her plastic surgery. In October, after gracing the cover of The Cut, she revealed she had work done following the birth of her second child, which the publication then specified as a boob job. One year earlier, the actress told The New Yorker, “Everything bounced back, pretty much, after the first one. Second one, nothing bounced back.”.

While fans aren’t exactly sold on Lawrence’s denial of a bleph, makeup artists often do have tricks up their sleeves for faking an eyelid lift. For starters, placement matters. When emphasizing the crease, apply shadow above the natural crease. “I like patting shadows onto the lid first, then blending the edges after. Too much back-and-forth blending can make the shape disappear,” celebrity makeup artist Christian Briceno previously told Bazaar. Also, opt for an elongated look, like a soft wing, to make the eye look instantly bigger. This also applies to mascara—artists recommend focusing application on the outer corners versus the center.

Breaking: 15 Places to Donate This Holiday Season

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The act of gift-giving always seems incredibly fun before the holidays come around.
  • According to recent reports, that’s why, in recent years, I’ve made the decision to donate to an notable cause in a loved one’s name—and I’ve never, ever regretted it.
  • It has been revealed that “I always give to the Red Cross in the wake of natural disasters, but this year the cause was a little closer to home when the organization stepped in to provide relief to those displaced by the terrible building collapse that took place in Flatbush earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The act of gift-giving always seems incredibly fun before the holidays come around. But I doubt I’m the only one who has suddenly come to in a sweaty, consumerist panic after all the presents are unwrapped and there is wrapping paper and ribbon on the floor, wishing I’d put my money somewhere meaningful instead of showering my little cousins with books they are exceedingly polite about but clearly hate.

According to recent reports, that’s why, in recent years, I’ve made the decision to donate to an notable cause in a loved one’s name—and I’ve never, ever regretted it. Below, find a roundup of some of the Vogue staff’s favorite organizations doing hard and necessary work that could use a little love this holiday season:.

It has been revealed that “I always give to the Red Cross in the wake of natural disasters, but this year the cause was a little closer to home when the organization stepped in to provide relief to those displaced by the terrible building collapse that took place in Flatbush earlier this month. I live near the building site, and for several nights, the entire neighborhood was kept awake by hovering helicopters, a terrible reminder of the tragedy that had occurred. There have been many initiatives since, organized by friends and neighbors, to provide assistance. But for those who might like to bolster the resilient spirit of New York City this holiday season from farther afield, a donation to the Red Cross would be worthwhile.” —Chloe Schama.

Sources indicate that “As someone who has always loved reading, I believe books have the power to open up new worlds, spark our imaginations, and inspire us to dream bigger. Every child deserves the opportunity to experience that same magic. Behind the Book brings diverse books and authors into underserved New York City public school classrooms, helping children discover the joy of reading and storytelling.” —Molly Barstein.

Imagine a ticking clock: One person is diagnosed with cancer every 1.6 seconds worldwide, and the Breakthrough Board is a women’s coalition that has been funding life-saving cancer research at the University of Chicago for nearly 80 years. Vogue senior digital line editor Jane Chun recommends donating and/or volunteering your time for this worthy cause.

Many of us would be at a loss without our furry companions, so a donation to this animal welfare organization—which operates the largest no-kill animal shelter in the US in Kanab, Utah, and partners with shelters and rescue groups nationwide—is a particularly nice way to honor the beloved pet in your life.

United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has detained over 8,000 children and increased family separations under the Trump administration. A donation to this California-based nonprofit (which will be matched through the end of December) helps to support those children and families with critical legal resources, medical and psychological treatment, and other forms of sorely needed support.

Recent findings suggest that this nonprofit organization, which will have Vogue Head of Editorial Content Chloe Malle’s support this year, has been helping people affected by conflict and disaster around the world for the past 90 years. It is presently matching donations for families in Gaza (times three) through Giving Tuesday.

Over 10 million older adults live in poverty in the US, and this organization—which was founded by a Philadelphia social worker in 1954—works to mitigate that sad state of affairs by delivering healthy, culturally sensitive meals (and needed social contact) to seniors around the country.

A donation to this organization attempting to find a cure for multiple myeloma (a type of blood cancer that forms in plasma cells) goes particularly far right now, notes Vogue Fashion Commerce Director Madeline Fass, as every dollar you give before December 31 will be doubled—up to $1 million—thanks to a special matching challenge from Dr. Elsey’s Fund to Cure Cancer.

With ICE raids and arrests ongoing all over the country, a donation to the Los Angeles-based National Day Laborer Organizing Network’s Immigrant Defense Fund helps to support legal defense and public advocacy for immigrant communities under attack.

The right to a safe, accessible abortion has only become more imperiled since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022, and this nonprofit network of over 100 independent, grassroots abortion funds is working to increase access and make sure no pregnant person is forced to go without potentially lifesaving care.

According to recent reports, federal funding for NPR, PBS, and local public media stations was ended by President Donald Trump in 2025, but you can step up and help fill the gap by donating directly to your local station to support independent journalism. “I strategy to support my local NPR station, WNYC,” says Chloe Malle.

Nobody should be forced to navigate the aftermath of sexual assault or misconduct alone, and a donation to the Rape, Abuse & Incest National Network (RAINN) helps fund vital services like the organization’s national 24-hour sexual assault hotline to ensure that survivors always have somewhere to turn.

According to recent reports, there are tons of great organizations working to end hunger in the US, from Feeding America to Feed the Children, but sometimes it’s nice to find one working locally. For Newly introduced Yorkers, that might just be this Harlem-based nonprofit that serves 900 free, chef-prepared meals a week to community members facing hunger.

It’s a scary time for trans, nonbinary, and gender-nonconforming youth in the US, which makes a donation to this mutual aid project serving unhoused and/or vulnerable trans youth (or a gift purchased directly from someone’s registry) particularly meaningful.

“I initiative to adopt a couple of snowy owls for the children in my life through the World Wildlife Fund,” says Malle—and you, too, can help prevent the vulnerable species’s extinction (while nabbing yourself a snowy owl plush toy) by donating to the WWF.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Being a professional athlete takes an inordinate amount of hard work and dedication, which is why Trinity Rodman’s romance with Ben Shelton makes so much sense.
  • In November 2026, multiple outlets, including People, reported that the pair had broken up.
  • Industry observers note that rodman is prolific on TikTok, with more than 305,000 followers as of August 2025.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Being a professional athlete takes an inordinate amount of hard work and dedication, which is why Trinity Rodman’s romance with Ben Shelton makes so much sense. While Rodman is a soccer star, playing for the Washington Spirit and the United States women’s national soccer team, Shelton is a professional tennis champ, representing the U.S. at tournaments across the globe, including Wimbledon. Since making their relationship public in spring 2025, interest in Shelton and Rodman’s connection has only intensified.

In November 2026, multiple outlets, including People, reported that the pair had broken up. Here’s what you need to know about Rodman and Shelton’s relationship timeline.

Industry observers note that rodman is prolific on TikTok, with more than 305,000 followers as of August 2025. As a result, it makes perfect sense that the star athlete appeared to tease her new romance with Shelton on the platform. The pair hinted that they were both “shooting their shot” with one another in a TikTok trend in March 2025, via espnW’s Instagram account. And it wasn’t long before the two athletes decided to hard-launch their romance on social media.

On March 18, Shelton shared a series of photos on Instagram, the last of which was a mirror selfie taken with Rodman in an elevator. “I been focused, but I’m steady climbin’, I’m nowhere near my peak,” he captioned the post. The soccer player commented on her boyfriend’s post, writing, “Shooters shoot I guess,” suggesting that the TikTok most certainly paid off, as reported by The Mirror US.

After Shelton and Rodman revealed their relationship on Instagram, tennis pro Frances Tiafoe suggested he was actually responsible for introducing the pair. During an appearance on the TikTok account Overtime Tennis on March 18, 2025, Tiafoe mentioned, “By the way, I don’t think people realize, I was like, the one who [connected them]—if we’re going to be real.”.

In a recent development, “I’m happy for him, man,” Tiafoe said of Shelton. “The elevator photo out the gate...everybody knows who Trinity Rodman is. [The photo] at the end of the carousel, sick.”.

It has been revealed that however, Shelton and Rodman later denied Tiafoe’s version of events, suggesting he wasn’t responsible for them meeting. “I don’t know if I want everyone to know the story [of how we met], but I can assure you Frances was not the reason we met or got together. I don’t know why he’s taking credit for that,” Rodman told ESPN’s SportsCenter. “Me and Ben can both cut that out. It was solely a me and Ben thing.”.

In a recent development, shelton also shot down Tiafoe’s claims, telling the Newly introduced York Post, “We’d like talked about her once, twice before and I was like, ‘But come on, man. You didn’t do anything.’ Putting us together, like that’s a bit of a stretch.” He continued, “[Rodman] was kind of annoyed by that. She was like, ‘Come on, bro.’ I think she remarked something to him a couple times. But we’re all friends.”.

After Shelton took their relationship public with his March 18, 2025 Instagram post, Rodman returned the favor by posting an adorable photo on social media, too. The picture indicated Rodman gazing up at her tennis pro boyfriend, whose face was hidden by a baseball cap. Tagging Shelton in the photo, Rodman captioned her March 27 Instagram post, “Dibs.” Shelton commented on the post, writing, “Whoever that is he won [for sure].”.

Recent findings suggest that from that point on, the romance between the two athletes seems to have only grown stronger. For instance, in an Instagram carousel posted on April 5, 2025, Shelton shared a short clip as he walked alongside Rodman, captioning the post, “In n out of time zones,” suggesting they were traveling together.

The public’s excitement about the romance wasn’t lost on Rodman and Shelton. During an appearance on ESPN’s SportsCenter in March 2025, Rodman spoke about her decision to go public with the relationship, saying, “I mean, I’m just another person in a relationship and people know about it.” She continued, “I’m obviously very happy.”.

In his April 2025 interview with the New York Post, Shelton discussed his romance with Rodman, and the incredible response they had received after revealing their relationship on Instagram. “It’s been great, obviously,” the 22-year-old athlete remarked. “I guess I didn’t think it would blow up as much as it did. That’s not why I did it.”.

Industry observers note that the tennis pro also suggested that “posting your girlfriend on Instagram is a more normal thing,” so he didn’t necessarily think the photos would make such an impact. “I realized, ‘Wow, people care about my life that much,’” he told the outlet. “But yeah, [we’re] happy for sure.”.

The same month, Rodman shared a TikTok video of herself hugging her boyfriend, with the caption, “My safety blanket...you make everyday better.”.

In April 2025, celebrated Olympian Rodman traveled to Munich in support of Shelton, who made it all the way to the men’s singles final in the BMW Open 2025. Rodman made her debut in the player’s box when Shelton beat Francisco Cerundolo in the men’s singles semifinal, and was spotted talking to her boyfriend’s dad, Bryan Shelton, during the competition. “She’s a good luck charm,” @tennischannel wrote on Instagram. Although Shelton ultimately lost the final to Germany’s Alexander Zverev, Rodman’s presence at the tournament made their relationship status quite clear.

It has been revealed that in July 2025, Shelton made it to the quarterfinals at Wimbledon, where he ultimately lost to Italian tennis player Jannik Sinner. Rodman supported her boyfriend at the tournament in London, and she also criticized commentators for calling her the wrong name and mentioning her estranged dad, former NBA player Dennis Rodman.

Recent findings suggest that “For those who don’t know...my name is TRINITY not Tiffany,” Rodman wrote on her Instagram Stories, via Sports Illustrated. “Also, for Ben’s matches he has his family there as his support system, which includes his dad... my dads not even in MY life no need to bring him up during HIS matches when I don’t even want him talked about during mine.”.

According to recent reports, as well as competing across Europe throughout the summer, Shelton still found time to savor some vacation days with his girlfriend. On May 20, Shelton shared two sweet photos on Instagram, which he captioned, “Happy birthday beautiful girl...I love you.” The Olympic gold medalist responded in the comments, writing, “I luhhh you.”.

The following month, Rodman shared footage showing her holding hands with her boyfriend as they walked around Europe. “No one else,” she captioned the Instagram post. On July 5, the Washington Spirit player shared another cute photo with Shelton, with the caption, “Watching you with googly eyes,” to which he responded, “Why am I cheesin so big.”.

Recent findings suggest that as both Shelton and Rodman are accustomed to traveling the world for their careers, they’ve had to adjust to dating while being in completely different places. “It has its challenges, but it’s definitely worth it,” Shelton told Town & Country. “It’s not something that we’re not used to—it’s been the story of our lives, especially me being on the road all the time. It’s just normal life stuff.”.

In August 2025, Rodman made her long-awaited return to soccer after taking time off to deal with a back injury. Prior to returning to work, Rodman shared vacation snaps with Shelton, along with training videos, writing on Instagram, “Not the summer that I had in mind but still loved every moment...can’t wait to be back on the field.”.

It has been revealed that on August 3, Rodman’s team, the Washington Spirit, played against the Portland Thorns in the National Women’s Soccer League. After joining the game for the final 14 minutes, Rodman was able to score the winning goal, cementing her triumphant return to the sport.

Shelton wasn’t able to support his girlfriend in person, as he was in Toronto for the 2025 National Bank Open. However, he celebrated her win from afar, telling ATP Tour, “One year anniversary from her incredible goal at the Olympics, hadn’t played in 100-something days and she goes in and in 15 minutes scores a banger. It’s pretty cool, especially [because] she was emotional. I’m always happy for her.”.

On June 14, Rodman shared a selfie with Shelton on Instagram, writing simply, “#1 fan I love you ❤️.”.

Rodman traveled to Montreal to surprise Shelton during the Canadian Open after playing with the Washington Spirit in Washington, D.C., on August 8. She documented his reaction on her Instagram Stories, writing, “Surprised his ass, happy matchday in Montreal 😘❤️ @benshelton.”.

It has been revealed that shelton went on to win the tournament, and Rodman celebrated his victory in an August 14 Instagram post. Alongside a photo of the couple walking together on the tennis court, she wrote, “Drive, dedication, and commitment. Back to back Canada champ! Celebrate every win baby ❤️ I love you.”.

During an August 2026 appearance on Kylie Kelce’s Not Gonna Lie podcast, Rodman opened up about how her relationship with Shelton began, revealing that she was the one who initially reached out.

“Everything I do is just embarrassing. I’m really embarrassed,” she stated.

Rodman explained just how promptly she wanted to get to know Shelton: “I fully committed to this guy that I didn’t even meet yet, for him to stay at my house for the weekend. It’s actually crazy, it’s insane, but it worked out.”.

She also discussed why she personally embraces being called a WAG despite being a professional athlete herself.

“For me, I think I like the term personally because, like I said before, I feel like 24/7 I’m on in front of cameras…and so I think I use the term WAG for me to simplify what I’m doing,” she said. “For me, saying WAG, it’s me being like, ‘I’m Ben’s girlfriend.’ But I can understand why [the term] is so hated.”.

Rodman added that having a partner who understands the demands of professional sports has been particularly meaningful to her.

Industry observers note that “It’s the best feeling in the world, honestly. I think to know we’re both on the grind, running our bodies to the ground, always exhausted, doing what we love, and then to also be able to be a little like a WAG in a sense, it feels so good for us,” she said.

Recent findings suggest that rodman showed her support for Shelton after he beat Carlos Alcaraz in the quarterfinal of the US Open. The competitive match ended at 3:30 A.M. “My 🌎,” she wrote on her Instagram Story.

She was also in the stands cheering him on:.

On November 24, People reported that the couple had broken up. Days before, Shelton responded “no” when asked if he would attend Rodman and the Washington Spirit’s championship game against the Kansas City Current on November 21.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders.
  • According to recent reports, “Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions.
  • Recent findings suggest that once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that I’m curled up on a treatment bed in the Corinthia spa, feeling a knot of tension dissipate slowly from my neck and shoulders. Within minutes, tears prick my eyes. I’m familiar with the sudden catharsis bodywork can bring, but this is different. Known as “myofascial release”—a targeted therapy that works with fascia, the continuous matrix of connective tissue that wraps every muscle, nerve, and organ—it aims to reduce tightness and release restricted tissue, restoring its natural glide.

According to recent reports, “Fascia is deeply connected to the entire sensory network,” explains Nadia Alibhai, a London-based osteopath who was unfazed by my heightened emotions. “When you move or hold stress, forces are transmitted through this interconnected system. It senses everything and dictates how the whole body responds. This treatment directly influences how we perceive and react to tension.”.

Recent findings suggest that once dismissed as mere biological wrapping paper, fascia—made up of water, collagen, elastin, and hyaluronic acid—is now understood as a living, three-dimensional web. “It’s part of a complex system involving movement, circulation, lymphatics, posture, and tissue health,” Alibhai explains. When it works well, it keeps everything moving and prevents systems from becoming sluggish, but when it becomes restricted, often from scrolling, sedentary habits, or chronic stress, the fluid between the layers can thicken. This affects physical mobility and emotional well-being, leading to issues ranging from pain and stiffness to a dysregulated nervous system.

Fascia and neurology are intrinsically linked, explains skin-health expert Annee de Mamiel. “Fascia changes according to how we move, breathe, and repeatedly load the body,” she states. “Cortisol and adrenaline change our physiology; the nervous system alters breathing, muscular tone, and stress response. Over time, these repeated patterns affect the tissues.” It’s a catch-22: greater stress can tighten fascia, which in turn can send your body into fight-or-flight mode, prolonging the anxiety that caused the damage in the first place.

It has been revealed that this mind-body connection is just one reason why fascia has piqued the wellness industry’s interest. Google searches for “fascia release” have soared in the past year, while facials targeting the system are becoming more popular. Robert Schleip, the director of the Fascia Research Group at Ulm University, attributes this to its holistic possibilities. “Fascia is now studied in relation to the autonomic nervous system, and therefore emotional regulation, as well as the immune system and aging,” he notes. The latest findings show that supporting your fascia goes far beyond easing a tight neck; it's linked to reduced arterial stiffness and improved cardiovascular health.

It has been revealed that fascia release has also entered the skin-health conversation. Tight fascia can be an overlooked culprit behind loss of luminosity, puffiness, and premature aging, states de Mamiel, because it’s heavily involved in fluid drainage and lymphatic pathways. “The diaphragm plays a role in pressure changes and fluid movement through the body, and the fascial system connects these areas,” she explains. “When I work on movement and tension through the neck, chest, and rib cage, I often see a change in how congested or puffy the face appears.” However, releasing fascia effectively doesn't require aggressive force. “If I use so much pressure that your body braces, I’ve produced the opposite response—it’s about creating conditions where the nervous system and tissue can both settle.”.

In a recent development, facialist Nichola Joss achieves similarly impressive results with her signature Inner Facial, which fuses lymphatic drainage, fascia release, buccal massage, and sculpting techniques. “Fascia surrounds and supports our muscles; when restricted, it affects how freely muscles move,” Joss explains. This affects lymphatic flow and your skin’s natural glow. “By releasing muscular and fascial tension, you lift, tone, and sculpt contours while boosting circulation and softening fine lines.”.

Beyond professional treatments, supporting fascial health depends on consistent daily habits. First, fascia thrives on varied movement: try walking, twisting your body, reaching overhead, and squatting to support overall health. Unfortunately, there are no true quick fixes: Spending the day glued to an office chair and then going straight into an intense HIIT session can actually be counterproductive. Instead, interrupt patterns throughout the day: Stand during phone calls instead of sitting, swing your arms gently during screen breaks, and make sure you’re not holding your breath during stressful periods at work. Counteract hours spent hunched over a device with this simple doorway stretch: Place your forearms against the frame, step forward gently, and hold for 20 to 30 seconds while breathing deeply.

Recent findings suggest that schleip recommends aligning exercise with your circadian rhythm. “Incorporate dynamic, elastic, or bouncing movements in the morning, ideally outdoors, and slow stretches in the evening,” he suggests, adding that sustained yoga positions, such as a child’s pose held for at least 30 seconds, can be particularly helpful. “Regular stretching improves joint mobility and may benefit cardiovascular markers such as arterial stiffness,” he adds. Finally, make nutrition and hydration a priority: fascia is 70 percent water and needs hydration to glide freely.

As Alibhai reflects at the end of my session: “The goal isn’t to constantly release fascia; it’s to keep your body moving, adaptable, and well nourished.” I leave feeling lighter and more grounded—and I instinctively skip the Tube and walk home.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you, like most people, hear the term “bourbon chicken” and have no idea what it is, let me call it by its more common name: toothpick chicken. Yes, the suspiciously delicious chicken shelled out at mall food courts on toothpicks is most likely bourbon chicken. Popular at American Chinese or Cajun-style Chinese restaurants, the sticky-sweet chicken is the utter definition of delicious, luring weary shoppers into food courts to find refuge from the bubblegum pink sweatpants and ripped denim. This version takes cues from the classic but swaps in some autumnal ingredients to make it fit for the season. Charred brussels sprouts leaves and pecans add bulk, while maple syrup and apple cider vinegar give it that delightful tart-sweet flavor we know and love. Serve it over rice or noodles or all by its lonesome for a hearty dinner that will take you back to the '90s.

More chicken dinner winners here: Sheet-Pan Hot Honey Chicken and Peaches; Basil Chicken Stir-Fry; and Ginger-Garlic Chicken and Vegetable Stir-Fry.

Whisk one 1½" piece ginger, peeled, finely grated, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, ⅓ cup bourbon, ⅓ cup pure maple syrup, ¼ cup apple cider vinegar, ¼ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes, 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, ¼ cup low-sodium soy sauce, and ½ cup water in a small bowl to combine. Set sauce aside.

It has been revealed that toss 1½ lb. skinless, boneless chicken breasts, halved crosswise, thinly sliced against the grain, remaining 1 Tbsp. cornstarch, and remaining 1 Tbsp. low-sodium soy sauce in a medium bowl until chicken is coated; set aside.

Heat 2 Tbsp. vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add 1 lb. brussels sprouts, halved through stems, leaves separated, and cook, stirring very occasionally, until just tender and blackened in spots, about 5 minutes. Transfer to another medium bowl.

Add more oil if pan looks dry and, working in batches if needed, arrange reserved chicken in a single layer and cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 minutes. Transfer to bowl with brussels sprouts.

It has been revealed that add reserved sauce to same pan and bring to a simmer. Cook, stirring constantly, until thickened, about 1 minute. Remove pan from heat and return brussels sprouts and chicken to pan; top with 1 cup salted roasted pecans, coarsely chopped. Toss to coat in sauce. Serve chicken and brussels sprouts with steamed white rice if desired.

Following the main character hat trend from a few seasons past, this time headwear has gone totally theatrical and over-the-top. Between Chanel’s fin-embellished Nemo-esque swim caps and Junya Watanabe’s super camp, oversize ’70s baker-boy-style caps, headpieces are seemingly obsessed with transforming their wearers into outlandish personas. Industry observers note that simone Rocha’s sequin-embellished bonnets with chin straps might turn you into a living doll. Ciara walked the Junya Watanabe spring/summer 2027 runway while wearing a bedazzled helmet dripping with chains.

Recent findings suggest that at Vaquera’s spring/summer 2027 show titled “I’m a put-on-a-show kind of girl,” the neon high-octane gowns were counterbalanced with huge, satirical boater hats, followed by a weird and whimsical chef hat and maid headpiece paired with shrunken, mini bloomer uniform onesies. Adding more humor to the collection, the designers ended the show by performing a live karaoke version of Sonny & Cher’s “I Got You Babe.” The brand is the king of the theatrical character hat. Can you be unhinged and complete at once? Its cast of characters—distorted drab mods, twisted ladies who lunch, abstracted leather daddies—all seem to suggest that the most covetable clothes for your future are those that mirror our fractured present.”.

While years of the past were defined by singular aesthetics, 2026 lacks one solo homogeneous style. Formality, too, has been traded for casual looks. Hats used to be ubiquitous; now they’re sort of a rare dying breed, save for a baseball cap.

Perhaps that’s one of the reasons why these character-driven hats are so prevalent now. Many of them are tied to uniforms, occupations, or the everyday made extreme. It’s beautiful absurdism, verging on delightfully unhinged. Consider an over-the-top hat pure whimsy.

  • More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that A traditional steak dinner can feel like too much for a weeknight: too expensive, too likely to trip the smoke alarm, too fussy to cook to a perfect medium-rare. But cut a steak into bite-size pieces and suddenly it transforms into a quick-cooking protein that’s no more demanding than chicken breast or tofu. Rub the steak with the spices and make the quick no-recipe yogurt sauce a few hours ahead if it’s helpful with time management. To account for the extra liquid thrown off by the spinach as it cooks, the water-to-couscous ratio in this recipe differs from that often found on the back of the bag (or box) so measure accordingly.

More quick dinners this way: Spicy Chicken Lettuce Wraps; Gochujang Chicken Stir-Fry; and Easy Fish Tacos With Spicy Sauce.

Recent findings suggest that place 1–1¼ lb. boneless New York strip steak (1–1½" thick), cut into 1" pieces, 1 Tbsp. dried oregano, 2 tsp. onion powder, 2 tsp. sugar, and 2 tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a medium bowl; season generously with freshly ground pepper and toss to coat. Let sit at least 10 minutes or cover and chill up to 8 hours (no need to bring to room temperature before cooking if chilling).

In a recent development, heat 2 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large high-sided skillet or medium Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid over medium. Add 1 bunch scallions, thinly sliced, ½ cup finely chopped dill, 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; cook, stirring occasionally, until scallions are softened, about 5 minutes. Add 10 oz. baby spinach in 2–3 handfuls, stirring and letting wilt slightly after each addition before adding more, 5–7 minutes total. Pour in 1 cup water and bring to a boil; season with more salt if needed. Add 1 cup Moroccan couscous and stir to break up any lumps. Remove from heat; swiftly cover with lid and let sit 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat 1 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil in a large skillet, preferably cast iron, over high. Arrange steak in a single layer; cook, undisturbed, until deeply browned underneath, 6–8 minutes. Reduce heat to medium; continue to cook, stirring often, until meat is just cooked through, about 1 minute more. Remove from heat. Add remaining 3 garlic cloves, finely chopped, and a large pinch of kosher salt; toss to combine. (Residual heat from pan will cook out any raw garlic flavor.).

Industry observers note that uncover couscous and fluff with a fork to separate grains. Spoon into a large shallow bowl or onto a platter. Top with steak. Cut 1 lemon into quarters and squeeze juice from 1 quarter over steak. Scatter thinly sliced cucumber and some dill sprigs on top; drizzle with oil.

Recent findings suggest that combine 1 cup plain whole-milk yogurt and a generous pinch of kosher salt in a small bowl; squeeze juice from 2 lemon quarters into yogurt. Stir to combine. If sauce is thick, stir in water, a spoonful at a time, to loosen.

Serve steak and couscous with yogurt sauce and remaining lemon quarter and more lemon wedges for squeezing over.

#146444. Breaking: I Tested Peloton's Newly introduced, More Affordable Folding Treadmill

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1660 w)

Breaking: I Tested Peloton's Newly introduced, More Affordable Folding Treadmill

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1660 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that in my mind and, I think the minds of many others, Peloton has always been a stationary bike brand.
  • Sources indicate that nevertheless, Peloton actually has been making treadmills since 2018.
  • The newly introduced Tread Flex, however, heads in a slightly different direction.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that in my mind and, I think the minds of many others, Peloton has always been a stationary bike brand. The Bike, after all, was its first product, turning the Peloton name into a catch-all term for at-home cycling that we now hear everywhere, from broadcasts of the Tour de France and Giro d'Italia to television sitcoms. (A running gag online is that Peloton's upscale, soothing video workout content is worlds away from The Office's Dwight Schrute leading a group of stationary riders off an imaginary cliff.).

Sources indicate that nevertheless, Peloton actually has been making treadmills since 2018. The first Tread delivered the same proposition as the Bike: premium hardware that looks good enough to bring out of the basement, as well as access to interactive, instructor-led runs and HIIT classes on a big, immersive screen. Over the years, Peloton has brought improvements to that first Tread: larger screens, voice controls, AI-informed movement tracking for form analysis and coaching.

The newly introduced Tread Flex, however, heads in a slightly different direction. It has a simpler belt, simpler speakers, a smaller screen. It's $1,300 cheaper than the next step up, and $4,500 cheaper (!) than Peloton's slat belt-equipped Tread+ Vision. Its affordability isn't even its main selling point, however, because the Tread Flex has a nifty final trick: it folds up to save space.

Could these space and money-saving tactics make the Tread as popular as the Bike? Well, I run nearly every day, and ever since a tester Tread Flex indicated up at my door, I've been doing it indoors much more frequently. In my experience, here's what makes Peloton's latest worth considering.

Treadmills tend to have a problem that stationary bikes don't: the nicer they get, the bigger they get. Premium models have larger motors and roomier running platforms. In short, they're heavy. (The Tread+ Vision is a hefty 460 pounds.) The Tread Flex is 170 pounds less, and that's crucial to its ability to fold up, because that feature wouldn't be much of a selling point if it felt like adding a power clean to the end of every run.

In reality, stowing the Tread Flex is quite easy. You just lift up the running deck from the end and push it forward until a hydraulic cylinder locks into place. There's a pin clip to lock it. To drop it down, you push forward on the deck and then on the hydraulic support, then walk it back. At about 45 degrees, the hydraulics take over completely; you can go put on your running shoes while a gentle thump lets you know the deck is back on the ground.

In a recent development, folding up the Tread Flex drops its area from about 16.5 square feet to half that. (The Tread+ Vision is around 19.25.) Just as importantly, I've discovered, is that lifting the deck brings the machine up onto a set of locking wheels. I've kept mine in a designated corner, but it's so easy to move that it wouldn't be much hassle to wheel it out and lower it for every workout, if your space required it. Get your cardio out of the way, then get your cardio out of the way.

Okay, so folding and moving a treadmill might be a pain if you're using it every day. But I suspect if you're running that often, you're doing some of it outside. I live less than an hour away from the Canadian border, and run on roads and trails five or six times a week all year round. Good layers get you pretty far, and there's a reason why run clubs continue to boom while SoulCycle-adjacent Mile High Run Club closed all its studios this year.

Treadmills are for something else. They're for a warm-up prior to lifting, or for bootcamp-style HIIT workouts that combine sprinting intervals with weight intervals. The prioritization value of time spent doing these doesn't seem to align with the space investment a treadmill requires if you don't have a pool house or major garage. (I have a sun porch-slash-mudroom where I keep firewood and ski boots in the winter and a napping couch in the summer.).

This is how, I think, the Tread Flex makes the ultimate proposition as the ideal home treadmill. A treadmill doesn't replace a usual running routine; it adds to it. On Monday I do my usual seven miles down the road and back on the river trails; on Tuesday I let Andy Speer kick my ass with sprints and kickstand deadlifts. (And, sure, when it's -10° and blowing in late January, I might run inside, now that I have the option.).

None of the above would matter as much if it came at the cost of quality. I've run on hotel treadmills that sound like your grandma's washing machine and feel similar to how they look, i.e., stomping around on hollow plastic. The Tread Flex may not have the cushioned slat belt the Tread+ Vision has, but it's definitely not that.

What it does have is a spec that's right in line with top-notch treadmills. Its max speed is 12.5 miles per hour (a 4:48 mile, in runner's units), a 12.5% max incline grade (but no decline), and a 20-inch by 59-inch running surface that, though not cushioned, feels good to run on. The swiveling screen is nice and significant at 21.5 inches, with HD resolution and a touchscreen interface. I particularly like how adjusting speed and incline is done with rolling knobs, which feel much better—and more natural—to engage with than buttons when you're gasping at threshold pace.

Recent findings suggest that on top of that is Peloton's interactive experience: You can take live classes where you can pit yourself against others and get kudos from the instructor. The pre-recorded catalogue includes thousands of classes for yoga, Pilates, and meditation, in addition to strength and the running, cycling, and rowing the company makes machines for.

The Tread Flex also provides personalized training looks, smart pacing guidance based on where you're at, automatically adjusting incline for classes, and of course leaderboards and an entire ecosystem of badges and achievements to earn, if you're into all that. For $50 per year, that is.

Oh, and did I mention it's a good-looking machine? It's sleek; an attractive, soft-edged Z with a minimal screen instead of a board of colorful buttons. Nobody's throwing around the word "console" to describe this thing. That's good; home gym setups deserve different consideration than gym rigs. If images of Crunch Fitness flash through your head every time you glance into the corner, something has missed the mark.

Recent findings suggest that where Peloton's Tread Vision treadmills are clearly high-end, the Tread Flex toes the line against mainstream consumer models. Its features match up with some of the most popular machines, and its price, while at the higher end of the spectrum, does too. But the Tread Flex gets there with more style, and with Peloton's huge ecosystem of live and archived class content.

Sources indicate that so, if we're looking at other treadmills out there, my quick answer is yes. The Tread Flex is the utilitarian Peloton Treadmill, but it's still a Peloton treadmill.

How you answer this question really requires asking yourself a series of other questions first. What do you want a treadmill for? How much do you want to invest? Do you want access to fitness classes—especially ones other than running—and are you okay with the $50/month subscription fee?

Form factor and access to classes and content are non-negotiables. The Tread Flex might be Peloton's upcoming entry-level treadmill, but it's far from a simple running machine. Flex refers to that nifty fold-up feature, but also to this treadmill's ability to integrate into an exercise program that also includes strength training, HIIT workouts, yoga, and on and on.

As a runner who prefers to log miles outside whenever possible, I was encouraged by how much I enjoyed running on the Tread Flex. The classes are fun, and Peloton's instructors are real pros, but even in Just Run mode, the Tread Flex proved responsive and comfy. It's getting dark around 4:30 PM these days, and my daylight windows for running on the well-used roads around me have narrowed like a Death Star trash compactor. It's nice to know I can snag seven miles after sundown if need be.

Well, if you aren't limited by space or cash, the Tread Vision and Tread+ Vision get you bigger screens, AI-enabled running form feedback and coaching, and a more cushioned, broader running area. If you just prefer running or walking on a treadmill to doing it outside, investing more heavily in a treadmill is worth considering (though the Tread Flex will still be great).

The Tread Flex's real competition is the NordicTrack Commercial 1750, which you'll find recommended on just about every treadmill buying guide on the internet. The machines are similar in function and specs, but there are some differences. The NordicTrack's running surface is two inches wider and one inch longer; it has a slightly more powerful motor; it can decline to -3% grade; its belt is slightly cushioned; it has a built-in fan; and NordicTrack's class and entertainment platform, iFit, is cheaper at $39 a month.

Industry observers note that in comparison, the Tread Flex takes up slightly less space, has a higher max speed (12.5 mph over 12 mph), a steeper incline (12.5% over 12%), and a larger screen (21.5 inches over 16 inches). The rolling knobs to adjust speed and incline are nicer to use. My partner, who designs commercial and residential interior spaces, agrees with me that the Tread Flex is a better-looking machine.

List price for the Tread Flex is $300 cheaper, but the NordicTrack seems to be perpetually on sale. So it might come down to looks, that 3% decline, or what class platform you'd like to buy into.

Like any specialized skill set, winter layering is one that must be continually practiced and perfected, lest your talents wane. It’s not as easy as throwing on a pair of cashmere leggings and a coordinating hoodie—that’s only the beginning. From there, it takes a careful curation of hero pieces (like puffer jackets and parkas), as well as a cast of supporting details (hats, gloves, and high-performance footwear), to layer effectively and aesthetically in the harshest conditions.

Recent findings suggest that that stated, even the most adept artist is nothing without an arsenal of trusted creative tools. And in these bitter temps, you’ll want to reach for the best, which essentially means any piece of gear with The North Face’s iconic rectangular logo attached to it. The storied brand has dominated the outdoor space for decades, having perfected the art of elevated style at elevated altitudes.

Industry observers note that as we head into the chilliest season of the year, look to The North Face’s vast selection of dependable staples for all your layering needs. Designed both for performance and appearances, these pieces are in it for the long run.

Sources indicate that whether painting or dressing, it’s essential to start any creative endeavor with a blank canvas made of quality materials. A good base should be versatile and simple to pair with a host of helpful staples. Long-sleeve tees, cashmere turtlenecks, and crewneck sweatshirts, for example, are all good jumping-off points.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for a high-performance piece with enough style power to stand on its own, we recommend the Women’s Chabot 2.0 Mock-Neck. This cozy layering top offers the same reliable comfort of a traditional insulated thermal with a few modern updates. Though understated by design, its delightfully oversized fit and a funky waffle knit texture make the basic feel intentional and interesting.

In a recent development, for a closer-fitting base, the Women’s Golden Ridge Ribbed Long-Sleeve Tee layers easily under other pieces. Its slim fit and ribbed texture give this practical layer a polished look, while thumbholes at the cuffs add a functional detail. Bonus points for the tee’s anti-odor technology that helps keep the fabric feeling fresh.

Women’s Golden Ridge Ribbed Long-Sleeve Tee.

Recent findings suggest that after you’ve selected the first layer, the next stop should be your coat closet. This is where you’ll select the hero of your look. While each piece of the layering puzzle is uniquely notable, the power jacket is a non-negotiable. The right iteration should supply a thick layer of warmth, while also doing its part to make the outfit, as a whole, feel cohesive.

Those who crave a more subdued winter aesthetic will love the classic appeal of the Women’s Arctic Bomber. The waterproof winter jacket boasts all the utility of a parka, with the sleek design details most commonly found in trend-focused outerwear. In four comforting colorways, this winter coat is an insulation powerhouse in a chic, wearable package.

Look to the Women’s Hydrenalite Down Jacket for a more classic puffer. This workhorse is a versatile down layer that can be slipped on at any time to keep you warm for any duration that you spend outdoors, whether you are on the mountain or running around town.

Sources indicate that for the more artistically inclined, try the Women’s Yumiori Off Peak Full Zip Jacket. This fleece outer layer offers unfailing warmth and a distinctly sporty flavor. Its two-tone color palette, meanwhile, adds a fun, whimsical feel to the utilitarian, zip-up-style silhouette.

Women’s Hydrenalite Down Jacket.

Women’s Yumiori Off Peak Full Zip Jacket.

In a recent development, during the summer months, it’s all about the mani-pedi. But once that icy weather blows in, self-care starts to look a bit different. The North Face’s Etip Gloves are basically a hand treatment on the go. Crafted from soft, stretchy fleece made with 93 percent recycled polyester, these tech-friendly gloves will keep your hands comfortable on cold-weather outings. They’ll also keep you connected: Touchscreen compatibility lets you check your phone without taking them off, while silicone grip dots on the palms help you hold onto your device as well as smaller essentials like keys and credit cards.

Industry observers note that for footwear, the Women’s THERMOBALL Traction Mule V will quickly become the standout of your seasonal lineup. These cloud-like slip-ons pair warm insulation with a quilted upper that gives them a casual, streetwear-cool vibe. The rubber outsole adds traction for quick trips outdoors.

Women’s THERMOBALL Traction Mule V.

It has been revealed that the minimalist philosophy requires you to take off one item before leaving the house. But during the cold weather season, it’s in your best interest to do the opposite. As you walk out the door, make sure you grab a beanie since most of your body heat can escape from your head.

Beanies are simultaneously the most underappreciated outfit addition and the most indispensable. The North Face’s Wool Blend Beanie, for instance, pairs the warmth of its 65 percent merino wool knit with a refined, metropolitan style. Its classic cuffed design and textured knit add visual interest, while its deep fit offers roomier coverage. If you prefer the rectangular logo with the same cuffed look, you can never go wrong with the rib-knit and soft lining of the Salty Lined Beanie. On the slopes or on your morning commute, either will add a polished finishing touch.

The importance of a functional winter hat cannot be overstated—think of it as the final brushstroke in the art of winter layering.

Mussels With Garlicky Miso Broth

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (401 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that mussels deserve your attention on weeknights.
  • According to recent reports, the seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home.
  • More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that mussels deserve your attention on weeknights. An affordable and accessible protein, they also happen to cook in less time than it takes to boil water. As the bivalves steam, they release a briny liquid, further perfuming the buttery, sake-fortified miso broth. Load up each bowl with a few good ladles, slurping every drop with an assist from crusty bread or warm rice. And why not enjoy the rest of the bottle of sake alongside your meal?

According to recent reports, the seafood counter at your supermarket should sell rinsed and debarred mussels, but it’s easy to do at home. Discard any with cracked shells. Gently tap open raw mussels on a counter to see if they slowly close; if they do, those are okay to use. Swish them in a water-filled salad spinner or colander fitted inside a bowl, draining and refilling until water runs clear (give any especially dirty ones a scrub with a sponge). Use a towel to pull off the fibrous beard and set on a towel-lined tray in the fridge until you’re ready to cook.

More seafood dinners this way: Avgolemono Seafood Stew; Spaghetti alle Vongole; and Gorgeous Green Shrimp.

It has been revealed that place 2 Tbsp. scallions from 8 scallions, thinly sliced on a diagonal, in a small bowl and set aside for serving.

Recent findings suggest that melt 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add 8 garlic cloves, thinly sliced, and remaining scallions to pot and cook, stirring often, until softened, about 4 minutes. Add 2 Tbsp. white miso paste and ½ tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) and cook until miso is broken up and incorporated into butter, about 20 seconds. Pour in 1 cup dry sake or dry white wine and stir to combine, then add 3–3½ lb. mussels, scrubbed, debearded. Cover pot and increase heat to medium-high. Cook, shaking pot occasionally, until mussels open, 5–7 minutes (discard any that do not open). Remove pot from heat.

Recent findings suggest that squeeze 1 lemon half over mussels. Cut remaining 1 lemon half into wedges for serving. Taste broth and season with kosher salt if needed.

In a recent development, ladle mussels and broth among shallow bowls, then scatter reserved scallions over. Serve with country-style bread or steamed white rice if desired and lemon wedges for squeezing over.
